Mr. Sheikh Muhd. Serajul Islam, Advocate ------ For the petitioners
Mr. Md. Abdul Khaleque, A.A.G. ------ For the State
parties:
A. Halim and another
Vs.
The State
full_judgment:
3. The investigating officer investigated the case and submitted charge sheet against the accused-petitioners under 326 and 448 of the Penal Code. The Additional District Magistrate, Dhaka framed charge against the convict-petitioners under section 326 and 448 of the Penal Code. The prosecution examined as many as 6 witnesses to prove the case. The Magistrate upon consideration of the evidence on record found the accused-petitioners guilty under section 326 of the Penal Code and sentenced them to suffer R.I. for one year each and to pay a fine of Tk.2,000/-, in default, to suffer R.I. for a period of one month more by the judgment and order dated 16.03.2003. 

 8. Mr. Sk. Muhd. Serajul Islam, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the convict-petitioners has taken me through the FIR, charge sheet, deposition of witnesses, Medical certificate, impugned judgment and submits that the occurrence allegedly took place on 30.01.1992 but the FIR was lodged on 02.02.1992 after 3 days without any satisfactory explanation, as such the case is highly doubtful. He submits that the prosecution withheld some important witnesses without any explanation, had they been examined they would not have supported the prosecution case as such the defence is entitled to get benefit of 114(G) of the Evidence Act. The learned Advocate submits that the victim Sadar Ali (P.W.3) deposed in the trial Court that he got injury on two fingers of his left hand, but the doctor (P.W.6) deposed mentioning the ring finger of his right hand was found to have been damaged as such the evidence of P.W.3 and P.W.6 are highly contradictory to each other which has created serious doubt about the veracity of the occurrence. He further submits that the trial Court and the appellate Court without appreciation of the evidence on record most illegally held the convict-petitioners guilty under section 326 of the Penal Code, as such the Rule should be made absolute. 

 9. Mr. Md. Abdul Khaleque, the learned Assistant Attorney General appearing on behalf of the State-opposite party submits that both the trial Court and the appellate Court after assessment of the evidence on record rightly found the accused-petitioners guilty under section 326 of the Penal Code as two fingers of victim Sadar Ali was dislocated by ramdao-blow, as such there is no ground to interfere in the judgment. He submits that on the date of occurrence victim Sadar Ali was shifted to Dhaka Medical College Hospital for treatment where P.W.6 Dr. Azizur Rahman Khan found five injuries on his person which were grievous in nature, as such there is no reasonable ground to interfere in the order of conviction and sentence under section 326 of the Penal Code. He further submits that the defence has not been prejudiced for non-examination of the investigating officer, as such the Rule having no substance is liable to be discharged. 

 10. Now let us examine the evidence on record for its critical analysis. 

 11. P.W.3 Sadar Ali, the victim of this case has stated that on 30.01.1992 at about 4 p.m. he along with Almas (P.W.2) and Jalil (P.W.4) were going to the paddy field and while they reached, near the house of Sanaullah at that time accused Khaleque and Halim armed with ramdao attacked him. Then he ran towards the house of Sanaullah and entering into a room shut the door but the accused-petitioners broke into the room and dragged him out of it and started to give ramdao-blow on his person successively as a result two fingers of his left hand were dislocated and he also received cut injuries on his waist and knee of left leg causing bleeding injuries and thereby became senseless. Thereafter his companions P.Ws.2 and 4 shifted him to Dhaka Medical College Hospital for treatment. He further stated that the accused persons demanded Tk.10,000/- as subscription but he refused to pay the same, for such reason he was assaulted by the accused persons on the date of occurrence. P.W. 6 Dr. Hafizur Rahman Khan stated that on the date of occurrence he was on duty in causality department of Dhaka Medical College Hospital on that day he examined victim Sadar Ali and found 5 injuries on his person which were grievous in nature. He proved his medical certificate containing his signature Exbt-2 and 2/1. From the evidence of victim Sadar Ali (P.W.3) it is found that he received cut injuries on his two fingers of his left hand but the doctor (P.W.6) has proved the injury certificate (Exbt-2) of P.W.3 stating that he found a injury on the ring finger of his right hand which contradicts with the evidence of P.W.3 as such the alleged injury received by the victim has not been proved beyond shadow of doubt. It further appears from the injury certificate (Exbt-2) that Sadar Ali received 4 injuries on his person which were incised wound, penetrating wound and lacerated injury on different parts of his body causing bleeding injury. From the evidence of P.W.3 Sadar Ali, it is well proved that at the time of occurrence accused-petitioner A. Khaleque dealt ramdao-blow successively on his person which caused all the injuries found in the injury certificate. P.W.3 has also stated that accused Halim gave him a ramdao blow on his right hand but he did not say whether he received any cut injury or not. 

 12. In view of the fact, I am of the opinion that the charge under section 326 of the Penal Code against accused Halim has not been proved beyond shadow of doubt. On the other hand it is well proved from the evidence on record that the accused A. Khaleque on the date of occurrence gave several ramdao blows on the person of Sadar Ali causing bleeding injury which has been also supported by medical evidence. It appears from the injury, certificate (Exbt-2) that the doctor found 5 injuries on the person of victim Sadar Ali but the cut injury on finger of victim Sadar Ali has not been proved beyond shadow of doubt. It appears that the rest 4 injuries were simple in nature. 

 14. Having regards to all facts and evidence on record, I am inclined to hold that both the trial Court and appellate Court without proper assessment of the evidence on record most illegally held both the accused-petitioners guilty under section 326 of the Penal Code which is not sustainable in law. I have already arrived at a dicision that the charge under section 326 of the Penal Code against convict-petitioner. A. Halim has not been proved as such he is entitled to get an order of acquittal.
